title: Local students lauded by council, school board
text:
The town council is encouraging all members of the community to extend “sincere congratulations” to students at every level who are moving forward with the class of 2026.
The councilors unanimously approved a proclamation at their May 18 meeting that declared June 15-18 as Graduates’ Week in Jamestown.
Councilwoman Mary Glackin read the proclamation, which said the council recognizes “the effort and perseverance that are necessary for the search for knowledge and excellence.”
“We applaud the achievements of all students associated with this community,” it says. “Graduation heralds not only the accomplishment of one level of that search but the commencement of the next; and this community, like all communities across the nation, will one day reap the harvest of the educational seeds of knowledge that are now being sown, when our students reappear as informed, involved community-minded citizens ready to take up the mantle of leadership in every field of endeavor.”
The councilors also noted their “deep and sincere appreciation” of the teachers “who have dedicated their lives and ambitions to the accomplishments and achievements of their respective students.”
Members of the school committee also acknowledged the graduates at their June 4 meeting followed by a round of applause. Committeeman Christian Cowen read the proclamation.
